data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the package files and found standard AUR packaging practices. The PKGBUILD pins a specific upstream git commit, uses standard cmake/make build steps, and contains no suspicious network activity, obfuscated code, or unexpected file operations. data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error (HTTP 400 API failure) in the qwen model during the full PKGBUILD review phase, not by a genuine security finding. Notably, the same qwen model had already successfully audited the PKGBUILD in the initial pre-download phase and found it safe. The deepseek model completed all reviews successfully and found the package safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model experienced API failure (HTTP 400) during full PKGBUILD review, though it had already successfully audited the file in the initial phase
learnings: Tool errors (API failures) should not override successful earlier audits of the same file; implement fallback to prior successful results
Consider implementing retry logic for transient API failures before marking a file as inconclusive
When a file is successfully audited in an initial phase, subsequent tool errors on the same file should not change the overall verdict
